explanations.answer: New heavens and a new earth
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. The LORD says, "For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth." (Isaiah 65:17) He doesn't say He'll patch up the old ones. He says He'll create new ones.

explanations.answer: A new temple and a new altar
explanations.explanation: I see why that one looks tempting. But a temple and an altar don't show up anywhere in this verse. The LORD says, "I will create new heavens and a new earth." The real answer is bigger than a building, and it's the whole sky and ground.

explanations.answer: A new king and a new kingdom
explanations.explanation: Close in size, but not what the verse says. The LORD never mentions a king here. He says, "I will create new heavens and a new earth." Nobody gets a crown in this verse, but the whole sky and ground get replaced.

Almost the opposite, friend. The LORD says, "The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind." So they don't keep coming to mind. I'll be honest, I misread a recipe card like this once and had to bake it twice.

Right, it's false. The LORD says, "The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind." That's what the text says, and it's the opposite of this statement. When the new heavens and new earth come, the old things aren't hanging around in anyone's thoughts.
That's right. The LORD says, "But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create." Forever is a long time to rejoice. I can't even keep a good mood going through one burnt tray.

A week of rejoicing sounds nice, but that's not the number. The LORD says, "be glad and rejoice forever in what I create." Seven days would run out and the verse doesn't stop at seven. It says forever.
That would put an end date on it, and the verse doesn't give one. The LORD says, "be glad and rejoice forever in what I create." There's no harvest in this line. It says forever.
Yes, friend. The LORD says, "I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people." So the LORD is the one rejoicing here. He's glad over the city and the people He's creating.
The nations aren't named in this verse. The LORD says, "I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people." The one who rejoices is the LORD Himself, and that's the part worth remembering.
No kings in this verse, friend. The LORD says, "I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people." The rejoicing comes from the LORD Himself. Nobody had to send in a royal invitation.

That's the one. The LORD says, "The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her." The city is Jerusalem, and those sounds are the ones that stop. I think that's a sound nobody will miss.

Those aren't the sounds the LORD says will stop. He says, "The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her." Weeping and crying are the sounds that go away from Jerusalem, so this isn't about the happy noise.

Nice thought, but no instruments come up in this verse. The LORD says, "The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her." Those are the sounds that go quiet. Keep the band out of it, friend.
Yes, a hundred. The LORD says, "For the youth will die at a hundred years." So in this picture, someone a hundred years old is still called a youth. I'm already tired just reading that.

Twenty is way too young for this verse. The LORD says, "For the youth will die at a hundred years." So the youth lives to a hundred, five times longer than twenty. It's a much bigger number than you'd expect.
Forty is a good guess but a little short. The LORD says, "For the youth will die at a hundred years." That's the number in the verse. Forty wouldn't even get the youth halfway there.
True, friend. The LORD says, "he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed." The verse puts it just like that. A hundred is the mark in this picture.

That one's actually true. The LORD says, "he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed." So the word accursed is right there in the verse. It's all part of how big a hundred years is in this promise.
That's right. The LORD says, "They will build houses and dwell in them." The ones who build the houses are the ones who live in them. I'd call that a fair deal.
Selling isn't in this verse. The LORD says, "They will build houses and dwell in them." They build and then live there. That's the whole plan.
No giving away here, friend. The LORD says, "They will build houses and dwell in them." The builders are the ones who dwell in the houses. Nobody walks off from their own front door.
Yes, a tree. The LORD says, "For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people." A tree can stand a long, long time. That's the picture He gives for His people's days.

Flowers are pretty, but they aren't in this verse. The LORD says, "For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people." The picture is a tree. Give me a tree over a flower any day, friend.
Clouds come and go, so that's not the picture here. The LORD says, "For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people." It's a tree He names, not a cloud.
Not quite, friend. The LORD says, "They will not labor in vain." So the work doesn't go for nothing. The verse says the opposite of this statement.
Right, it's false. The LORD says, "They will not labor in vain." The work counts. In verse 22 He says His chosen ones "will fully enjoy the work of their hands."

explanations.answer: They will be blessed by the LORD
explanations.explanation: That's right. The LORD says, "for they will be a people blessed by the LORD." That comes right after He says they won't bear children doomed to disaster. He adds, "they and their descendants with them."

explanations.answer: They will live behind strong walls
explanations.explanation: Walls aren't mentioned in this verse. The LORD says, "for they will be a people blessed by the LORD." The blessing is the reason the verse gives. Nobody had to call a contractor.

explanations.answer: They will have plenty of workers
explanations.explanation: Workers aren't part of the reason here. The LORD says, "for they will be a people blessed by the LORD." That blessing comes from the LORD, with their descendants included. No hiring needed.

It's the other way around, friend. The LORD says, "Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear." So He doesn't wait for them to finish. He answers before they even call.

Right, it's false. The LORD says, "Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear." He answers before they call, and hears while they're still speaking. I've been cut off mid-sentence plenty, but never by that kind of answer.
That's the one. The LORD says, "The wolf and the lamb will feed together." Normally a wolf and a lamb don't share a meal. In this picture they eat side by side.
The bear isn't named in this verse. The LORD says, "The wolf and the lamb will feed together." The wolf's partner here is the lamb. A bear would've made it a very different picture.
An eagle doesn't show up in this verse. The LORD says, "The wolf and the lamb will feed together." The animals feeding together are the wolf and the lamb. No birds were invited.
True, friend. The LORD says, "the lion will eat straw like the ox." That's a lion eating straw, same as an ox does. I'd like to see that one on the counter.
That one's actually true. The LORD says, "the lion will eat straw like the ox." It's right there in the verse. Picture a lion calmly eating straw next to an ox.
True, friend. The LORD says, "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain." Neither harm nor destruction, and it covers the whole mountain. That's how the passage ends.
That one's true. The LORD says, "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain." So no harm and no destruction, anywhere on it. It's right there in the last verse.
